python3 << 'PY'
import statistics

# 1979 data from treasury_bulletin_1980_03_page_88.txt
# Treasury bonds (column 10) and New Aa corporate bonds (column 11) for 1979
treasury_1979 = [8.43, 8.43, 8.45, 8.44, 8.55, 8.32, 8.35, 8.42, 8.68, 9.44, 9.80, 9.58]
corporate_1979 = [9.47, 9.52, 9.65, 9.69, 9.82, 9.51, 9.47, 9.57, 9.87, 11.17, 11.52, 11.30]

# 1984 data from treasury_bulletin_1985_03_page_48.txt
# Treasury and New Aa corporate for 1984
treasury_1984 = [11.82, 12.00, 12.45, 12.65, 13.43, 13.54, 13.36, 12.71, 12.42, 12.04, 11.66, 11.64]
corporate_1984 = [12.65, 12.80, 13.36, 13.64, 14.41, 14.49, 14.25, 13.54, 13.37, 13.02, 12.40, 12.47]

print("1979 Treasury:", treasury_1979)
print("1979 Corporate:", corporate_1979)
print("1984 Treasury:", treasury_1984)
print("1984 Corporate:", corporate_1984)

# Calculate Pearson correlation
def pearson_corr(x, y):
    n = len(x)
    mean_x = statistics.mean(x)
    mean_y = statistics.mean(y)
    
    numerator = sum((x[i] - mean_x) * (y[i] - mean_y) for i in range(n))
    denom_x = sum((x[i] - mean_x) ** 2 for i in range(n)) ** 0.5
    denom_y = sum((y[i] - mean_y) ** 2 for i in range(n)) ** 0.5
    
    return numerator / (denom_x * denom_y)

corr_1979 = pearson_corr(treasury_1979, corporate_1979)
corr_1984 = pearson_corr(treasury_1984, corporate_1984)

print(f"\n1979 correlation: {corr_1979}")
print(f"1984 correlation: {corr_1984}")

abs_diff = abs(corr_1979 - corr_1984)
print(f"\nAbsolute difference: {abs_diff}")
print(f"Rounded to 4 decimal places: {round(abs_diff, 4)}")
PY
